brief: The canvas displays a microscopic view of polished quartz, visualizing how light interacts with its internal crystalline structure. Colored diffraction gratings are visible, forming an intricate lattice of repeating rods. Light enters this system, causing the visible colors to fracture into multiple distinct beams. These beams continuously undergo a dynamic process of apparent re-bonding, creating complex, ephemeral interference patterns that shift and bloom across the surface of the quartz structure.

statement: This sketch visualizes the microscopic world of polished quartz, capturing how light interacts with its crystalline structure. The scene features a lattice of diffraction gratings—thin, rod-like structures that split light into colorful beams. These gratings are arranged in a three-dimensional space, creating an intricate network where light particles bounce around and create dynamic interference patterns. As the viewer's perspective rotates slowly through the space, these interactions produce shifting, blooming color patterns that evoke the ethereal beauty of crystalline light manipulation. The technique uses batched rendering to maintain performance while achieving the visual complexity of a highly detailed, animated crystal surface.
